 Singapore and the US agree to keep discussing Megaspeed as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal widens
 By Jun Yuan Yong  and  Eduardo Baptista 
 Monday, 16 Nov 2026
 | 9:02 PM MYT

 Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement that the US had provided little help in its investigation into Megaspeed. -- PHOTO: AFP
 SINGAPORE (Reuters): Singapore's government said on Monday it has agreed to continue discussions with the United States about Megaspeed, the company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal.
 The Singapore-based cloud-computing company has become a focal point of attention after reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, whom US authorities suspect of being a spy for Beijing.
 Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO of Nvidia last Thursday and Reuters has not been able to contact Alice Huang for comment.
 Singapore's Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo discussed Megaspeed with US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau during a visit to Washington last week, the ministry said in response to a Reuters query.
 "Minister Teo and Deputy Secretary Landau discussed the facts of the case and reaffirmed the commitment by both countries to continuing communications on issues of mutual interest, including on matters relating to Megaspeed," the ministry said.
 In October 2025, the New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether Megaspeed helped Chinese customers obtain Nvidia computer chips subject to Washington's export controls. China has denied the allegation and Megaspeed has not been found to have violated ​the rules.
 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Treasury, the Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative's Office had been in favor of putting Megaspeed on a trade blacklist for months, though the Commerce Department, which is in charge of the list, had not been.
 Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducts a "legitimate and lawful business."
 Singapore said last week that Alice Huang had previously served as Megaspeed's chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers. Police found insufficient evidence that she committed offences relating to suspected false declarations over server purchases, but warned her for knowingly providing inaccurate information that played down her role.
 Alice Huang was barred from re-entering Singapore, while investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals are ongoing, the home affairs ministry said.
 (Reporting by Jun Yuan Yong in Singapore and Eduardo Baptista in Shenzhen; Editing by Edwina Gibbs and Sharon Singleton) -- Reuters
